transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~53 minutes
Recording link: https://redwood-recordings.example/ff-20250722-7842
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Priya (CTO - Stellar), Ben (Security Eng), Hannah (IAM Lead), Carlos (Platform Ops)

Summary:
Quick security-focused session to align on SSO (SAML) & SCIM provisioning, how roles will map into Redwood's RBAC, and questions on audit logging / KMS. Decision to run a short SSO pilot with 3 users + 2 groups. Action items assigned at end.

Topics covered:
- SAML metadata and SP vs IdP initiated flow
- SCIM group sync behavior and attribute mapping (groups -> roles)
- Role hierarchy and least-privilege templates for prod vs staging
- Audit logs, retention, and SOC2 implications
- KMS / encryption key ownership and rotation

Notes / quick wins:
- Redwood can accept NameID persistent or email format; recommended persistent for cross-account mapping if they have multiple emails per user (Ethan)
- SCIM: Redwood supports full user/group push and incremental PATCH semantics; group-only sync is available
- Use group-to-role mapping to avoid per-user role assignment; keep few top-level roles (billing-admin, infra-admin, app-operator, viewer)

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, Ethan our SE is here for SSO/SCIM deep bits, Liam for ops/support. Priya, do you want to intro the Stellar team?
00:14 Priya: Yeah hi all, I'm Priya, CTO at Stellar Payments. We have Ben on security, Hannah on IAM, Carlos on platform. We want to lock down SSO and make sure role mapping doesn't give too much blast radius.
00:27 Ethan: Cool, yeah today's agenda is to align on SAML metadata exchange, figure out SCIM group->role mappings, and talk least privilege. Quick note — I'm going to show a sample role JSON in the follow-up, not sharing it live in this call.
00:42 Ben: Quick question before we dive, are we expecting customer-managed KMS keys or redwood-managed? That influences our compliance path.
00:51 Maya: Good point. We support both; many enterprises use customer-managed keys in the Private deploys, hosted can support CMEK with some enterprise add-on. We'll include the KMS options in the follow-up.
01:05 Hannah: For SCIM, we need to confirm group names sync exact or if we can map with a prefix. Our IdP uses prod- and staging- prefixes for groups.
01:17 Ethan: We support mapping rules — you can map group regex to a Redwood role. Example: ^prod-(.*) -> app-operator-prod. We will send an example mapping table.
01:31 Carlos: Does SCIM do membership-only sync or will it push user profile attributes (like phone, employeeID)?
01:38 Ethan: Both, the push can include standard attributes: userName, name, email, employeeNumber. By default we accept email as primary id; for enterprise we can switch to immutable employeeID if that's your source of truth.
02:01 Priya: On SAML — we'd prefer SP-initiated since we want to control session state from Redwood side, any blockers?
02:10 Ethan: SP-initiated is fine. We'll provide ACS (Assertion Consumer Service) URL and SP metadata. Important: pick a NameID format, persistent recommended. If your IdP only issues transient, we can still map on email but it's less stable.
02:29 Ben: What about group claims in the SAML assertion vs SCIM? Best practice?
02:35 Ethan: If you want real-time role changes, use SCIM for groups. SAML group claims are OK at login time but won't update an existing session. For role revocation we rely on SCIM sync or short session TTLs.
03:00 Hannah: Ok, so we do SCIM for groups and SAML for auth. On SCIM patches, does Redwood support the RFC PATCH operations or only replace?
03:10 Ethan: We support PATCH (add/remove) and full replace; some IdPs send only replace so we account for both. We'll include a note about idempotent behavior.
03:26 Maya: Jumping to RBAC — we recommend a small number of roles and use group-to-role mapping. Typical templates we show: viewer, app-operator, infra-admin, billing-admin. Do you have any custom roles you need?
03:40 Priya: We'll need a limited 'token-creator' role for developers that can spawn short-lived keys but not modify billing. Also an 'ops-runner' to deploy model routes.
03:50 Ethan: Sounds good. We usually advise "principle of least privilege": build from the minimal roles and add granular privileges only when necessary. We will send a JSON schema that shows role->permission bits.
04:05 Ben: Encryption - are runtime model caches encrypted at rest? I saw something about KV cache in the docs but not sure about encryption.
04:15 Ethan: Yes, caches are encrypted at rest in hosted, and in Private you can plug in your KMS. Note sometimes docs say KV cache, but that's internal naming — sorry if that was confusing in the docs.
04:33 Ben: For audit logs, what's the retention range and can we export to our SIEM?
04:41 Liam: We keep detailed audit logs per token/action; default retention is 90 days on hosted with add-on longer retention. We do push to external sinks — S3, Splunk, or your SIEM via push connector. We'll attach the retention SKU matrix.
05:06 Priya: SOC2 and ISO artifacts — can you provide the SOC2 type II summary and our security questionnaire answers?
05:14 Liam: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 summary pack in the follow-up and a pre-filled security questionnaire. For ISO we'll include the scope doc.
05:25 Hannah: Back to SAML specifics — will you accept group claims as array or space-delimited string? Our IdP uses a space-delimited group list in the group attribute.
05:36 Ethan: We parse both, but if you can change to arrays it's cleaner. We'll normalize on ingestion.
05:48 Carlos: How do we handle users with multiple accounts across environments? For example, one person is in prod-admin group and staging-viewer.
05:56 Ethan: We recommend environment-scoped groups and mapping regex to environment-scoped roles. Sessions are environment-specific; SCIM sync maps membership accordingly. We'll document an example.
06:15 Ben: Any gotchas with SAML NameID and email? If the NameID changes, do we create duplicates?
06:22 Ethan: If you rely on email and users can change email, that can create duplicates. Use an immutable employeeID as the primary identifier to avoid collisions if your IdP supports it.
06:36 Priya: For the pilot, we want to start with 3 users and two groups — test-prod-admins and test-prod-viewers. Hannah will provision those in IdP.
06:47 Hannah: Yep, I'll set them up. Also question on SCIM credentials — is there a unique SCIM token per integration?
06:55 Ethan: We issue a scoped SCIM token per tenant/integration. It can be rotated. We support SCIM tokens scoped for groups only if you need limited access.
07:08 Maya: Let's go through a quick hypothetical: Ben wants to revoke infra-admin immediately after an incident. How quickly does SCIM sync revoke access?
07:19 Ethan: SCIM incremental usually processes within 30s-2min depending on system load; but if you want guaranteed immediate revocation, we recommend a short session TTL and event-driven hooks we can configure to expire sessions on-demand.
07:40 Ben: Good. About audit logs for privilege changes — do you show who performed the change and the requestor metadata?
07:48 Liam: Yes, audit logs include actor, token id, IP, and the change payload. We do redaction for sensitive fields by default.
08:02 Priya: For KMS rotation — if we use customer-managed keys, what's the rotation window and how do you handle encryption during rotation?
08:12 Ethan: We support rotation via KMS re-encrypt flow; typical rotation window is configurable. During rotation requests are queued and data re-wrapped; there is a short window of increased CPU but no data loss. We'll include the technical note.
08:30 Hannah: One small thing — mapping nested groups into roles, does Redwood support nested group resolution? Our org uses nested groups heavily.
08:38 Ethan: We can expand nested groups if your IdP's SCIM exposes membership or if we query the IdP for group membership. In some IdPs you need to enable group expansion feature. We'll note that as a per-IdP capability.
09:02 Carlos: Any rate limits on SCIM when doing large syncs? We have ~10k users and several hundred groups.
09:10 Ethan: For large orgs, we recommend a staged sync strategy. Default SCIM rate limit is modest; for bulk syncs we provide a migration window and temporary higher throughput. We'll coordinate via support.
09:30 Priya: Ok, before we wrap, a quick note on least privilege: we want to ensure billing-admin cannot read secrets or deploy. How granular are permissions?
09:40 Ethan: Fine-grained. Permissions are action-based (read:secrets, write:deploy, admin:billing). Roles are sets of permissions and you can create custom roles. We'll send the role permission matrix.
10:02 Ben: One more question — how are audit logs signed or guaranteed tamper-proof? We're trying to meet stricter SOC2 evidence requirements.
10:10 Liam: Logs are stored with integrity checks, and for Private deployments you can ship logs to your own immutable storage. We also provide cryptographic signing for long-term retention on request. We'll include the doc.
10:34 Maya: Great. Let's recap: Maya sends SAML/SP metadata and test steps; Ethan sends SCIM mappings and patch/retry notes; Hannah provides pilot groups/users; Liam shares SOC2 + audit retention options; Ben confirms KMS plan.
10:50 Priya: Sounds good. Anything else?
10:54 Hannah: One small ask — can we see a sample role JSON that includes exact permission bits so we can review with compliance?
11:02 Ethan: Yes, that's in the action items. We'll attach a sample role JSON in the follow-up.
11:15 Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get pilot users in place by next week.
11:18 Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.

Post-call quick checklist (spoken):
- Confirm SCIM token rotation cadence (Ben)
- Provide pilot schedule and staging URL (Maya)
- Share SOC2 artifacts and ISO scope (Liam)

End of transcript.
